stories.title: Scappoose is going to the state final: 44-32 over Banks, and a rematch with Cascade Christian on Saturday
stories.summary: Scappoose scored on six of its eight drives to beat Banks 44-32 in the 4A semifinal at Hillsboro Stadium on Saturday — Elijah Greenan Biggs scored four times — and the Indians are headed to the state championship game for the first time since 2015, after four straight semifinal losses. The final is a rematch: No. 1 Cascade Christian, the only team to beat Scappoose this year (35-7 back on Sept. 4). Kickoff is 2 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28, at Cottage Grove High School.

stories.title: Rainier football went 7-3 behind a 2,300-yard junior running back
stories.summary: Rainier's football season ended in the playoffs at Culver, but the Columbians' 7-3 turnaround ran on junior Jayden Quevido's legs: 2,329 rushing yards and 31 touchdowns in nine regular-season games — about 259 yards a night — a year after Rainier went 3-6. The Columbians averaged 35 points a game under coach Mike King.

stories.title: St. Helens High renovation earns the district $89,059 from the PUD for energy savings
stories.summary: The rebuilt St. Helens High School campus is projected to save 294,467 kilowatt-hours a year — about what 22 county homes use — and Columbia River PUD has paid the district an $89,059 incentive for it. The savings come from the new heating and cooling system, LED lighting, hot water boilers and high-efficiency kitchen equipment installed in the bond-funded renovation.

stories.title: Rainier parents built a tool that shows how kids use AI on schoolwork
stories.summary: Rainier parents have launched GuideEd, a free tool that shows parents the patterns in how their kids use AI on schoolwork — the questioning and answer-seeking habits — without making them read every conversation. The idea is guided use instead of secret use: parents can see whether AI is becoming a crutch, and step in before it does.

stories.title: Would you rent a tractor from the conservation district? Columbia SWCD is asking
stories.summary: The Columbia Soil and Water Conservation District is surveying county farmers about a possible farm equipment rental program — the library-for-tractors setup Clackamas County's district already runs, renting no-till seed drills for $175 a day and spreaders and smaller implements for less. Columbia's short survey asks local producers what equipment would actually be useful; the district office is in St. Helens (503-433-3205).
stories.img_credit: Photo of a tractor on a plowed field in Yamhill County, Oregon, by Gary Halvorson, Oregon State Archives, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY (licensed photo, News Scout batch 2, 2026-11-23).

stories.title: A record El Niño is building. Here is what it means for a Columbia County winter.
stories.summary: The equatorial Pacific is running about 2.5 degrees warmer than normal, and federal forecasters give better than an 83 percent chance this El Niño stays strong or very strong through March — possibly the strongest since 1950. For Columbia County the outlook leans mild, with near-average rain and the Northwest's best odds of a warmer-than-average winter — plus the catch every strong El Niño winter here has delivered: one short, hard stretch of cold or ice, most likely in January. Plan for a mild winter, the forecasters say, and be ready for one bad week.
stories.img_credit: Photo of Multnomah Falls in the Columbia River Gorge nearly frozen, by the Oregon Department of Transportation via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 (licensed photo, News Scout batch 2, 2026-11-23).

stories.title: The Bad Art Show: St. Helens library's gloriously tacky trophy
stories.summary: The St. Helens Public Library's third annual Bad Art Show gave adults 45 minutes and a pile of leftover craft supplies to make something 'tacky, glittery, and completely useless' — then the public voted, the winner took home the Bad Art trophy, and every entry hangs in the library hallway through November. Go judge them for yourself.

stories.title: County auctions 31 odd lots — a burned-out mobile home, mineral rights and a landlocked parcel — with opening bids from $368
stories.summary: The county put 31 county-owned properties up for auction in the St. Helens justice facility lobby on Nov 17, from a burned-out double-wide on a floodplain lot in Vernonia to nine mineral-rights-only parcels in the hills west of Vernonia. Minimum bids were set at what the county is owed rather than market value — about $189,000 in minimums against $1.74 million in assessed value — and the county first published the wrong minimum bids and had to correct them.

stories.title: USDA-backed sawmill breaks ground in Clatskanie
stories.summary: Construction has officially begun on a new sawmill in Clatskanie, backed by $30 million in USDA-guaranteed financing for Clatskanie Scion LLC to expand Sheridan-based Myers Woodline. The mill is expected to create at least 35 jobs and start up in about 18 months — a rare new mill in a state that lost seven mills in 2024 alone.
stories.img_credit: Photo: Columbia County Spotlight (the story's own photo, via Oregon Civic Newsstand).

stories.title: The Christmas Ships are coming back — plus every confirmed holiday date in the county, in one list
stories.summary: The Tribune's running roundup of confirmed holiday dates is out: the Christmas Ships pass St. Helens on Dec 12 and Scappoose Bay on Dec 13, the Scappoose Spirit of Christmas Parade is Dec 5, and Michael Allen Harrison plays Columbia City on Nov 30. The Keep It Local Wonderland Bazaar lands Nov 28 with more than 40 local vendors and free Santa photos.

stories.title: Vernonia posts the county's biggest test-score jump — English proficiency up 13 points in one year
stories.summary: Vernonia School District posted the largest one-year gain of any district in the county on state tests: 45.1% of students met the English language arts standard last spring, up from 32.0% a year earlier. The jump earned Vernonia a state literacy-tour “model school” recognition, and the district shared the results with the community at an engagement night on Nov 18.

stories.title: Columbia River Treasures reopens in Rainier after a three-week closure
stories.summary: The Rainier vintage shop is back open after an unexpected three-week closure while the owners handled medical issues. The shop at 113 E 1st St is freshly stocked for the holidays, with vintage Christmas decor, stockings and Santa mugs alongside Pendleton mugs, cozy flannels, Carhartt hoodies, jeans and graphic tees. Open Saturdays and Sundays, 12 to 6 PM.
